clinician.trajectory_summary: A 31-year-old female smoker presented with a 7-week history of fever, night sweats, joint pains, myalgia, nasal congestion, dizziness, hearing impairment, conjunctival injection (episcleritis), maculopapular rash, and nodular tender lesions. Initial workup excluded common systemic vasculitis with negative ANA, ANCA, rheumatoid factor, anti-CCP, and complement levels. Audiometry confirmed bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. Biopsies from lower limb rash demonstrated perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate consistent with small- and medium-sized vessel vasculitis. Clinical features of audiovestibular involvement, ocular inflammation, systemic vasculitis, and negative autoimmune serologies together support the diagnosis of Cogan’s syndrome.
